title: The veil of the temple rent from the top to the bottom — the way into the holiest opened, and the Sabbath still kept (Exodus 26; Leviticus 16; Hebrews 10)
summary:
It ain't new. At his death the veil tore, and it tore from the top:

*And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51)

*And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.* (Luke 23:45)

The veil was Moses' veil, hung to divide the holy from the most holy where the ark stood:

*And thou shalt hang up the vail under the taches, that thou mayest bring in thither within the vail the ark of the testimony: and the vail shall divide unto you between the holy place and the most holy.* (Exodus 26:33)

And behind it only one man came, once a year, on pain of death:

*And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat.* (Leviticus 16:2)

The letter to the Hebrews says what the tearing opened, and names the veil for what it stood for:

*Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Yahusha (Jesus),* (Hebrews 10:19)

*By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;* (Hebrews 10:20)

His flesh torn, the way in laid open, and the tearing from the top down because it was the Father's hand and not a man's. Isaiah had set a torn covering on the same mountain where the feast is spread:

*And he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations.* (Isaiah 25:7)

What the torn veil does not mean is that the house or its service was done away. The women who watched him die kept the Sabbath that same week according to the commandment, and the apostles went on going up to the temple:

*And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.* (Luke 23:56)

The veil opened the way to the Father through the Son's flesh. It did not close the Torah. The same afternoon that tore the veil kept the commandment about the body on the tree, and the next day was a Sabbath kept.

3148.prose: Mark gives the same tearing in fewer words. The veil goes *in twain from the top to the bottom*, and Mark sets it right after Yahusha (Jesus) gives up the ghost. A tear that starts at the top is the Father answering the death, not a man's hand.
3148.phrase: the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom
3148.sentence: Mark tells the same tearing, from the top to the bottom, so the opening comes from above.

3149.prose: Luke tells it with the darkness first, *the sun was darkened*, and then the veil torn *in the midst*. Matthew says from the top, Luke says the middle. Either way the covering that kept the holiest shut is split open at the death of Yahusha (Jesus).
3149.phrase: the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst
3149.sentence: Luke sets the darkness and the torn veil together, the veil split in the midst at the hour of the death.

3150.prose: Here is the veil that tore. Moses was told to weave it in blue, purple and scarlet, and it hung between the holy place and the most holy. It was made *with cherubims*, and Matthew's tear runs through that very hanging. What Moses hung, the Father opens, and the Torah's house is entered, not thrown out.
3150.phrase: a vail of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen of cunning work
3150.sentence: This is the woven veil of blue, purple and scarlet that Matthew's tearing runs through.

3151.prose: The rule of the veil begins with a death. Aaron's two sons *offered before Yahuah (LORD), and died*, and the way behind the veil was fenced from then on. Then Yahusha (Jesus) dies and that same veil is torn from the top. The fence that death guarded is opened by a death.
3151.phrase: after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before Yahuah (LORD), and died
3151.sentence: The veil's rule begins with two sons of Aaron dead, which is why the way behind it was fenced.

3152.prose: Hebrews reads the tearing for us. The way into the holiest is *by the blood of Yahusha (Jesus)*, and the same writer goes on to call the veil his flesh. So the tear from the top is the way to the Father laid open, not the temple dismissed.
3152.phrase: boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Yahusha (Jesus)
3152.sentence: Hebrews says the torn veil opens boldness to enter the holiest by the blood of Yahusha (Jesus).

3153.prose: Hebrews names the one who goes through. Messiah (Christ) comes as high priest to a place *not made with hands*, and the veil torn from the top fits that, since no man's hand tore it. The way he takes leads into the Father's own presence.
3153.phrase: by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands
3153.sentence: The tabernacle not made with hands is the place the torn veil opens toward, entered by Messiah (Christ).

3154.prose: Hope reaches *that within the veil*, the very place the veil hid, where the ark stood. Yahusha (Jesus) went in there first as forerunner. When the veil tears from the top, that inner place is what lies open to the ones who follow.
3154.phrase: which entereth into that within the veil
3154.sentence: Hope enters the inner place behind the veil, the place the tearing lays open.

3155.prose: Because the veil is torn, the throne is near. *Come boldly unto the throne of grace* is said to a people whose high priest once went in alone, once a year, on pain of death. Now mercy is asked for at the very place the veil guarded.
3155.phrase: come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy
3155.sentence: The call to come boldly to the throne of grace is spoken at the place the veil once fenced off.

3156.prose: This is the fence the tearing answers. Aaron could not *come not at all times into the holy place* behind the veil, or he would die, because Yahuah (LORD) would appear in the cloud on the mercy seat. The torn veil opens that same place through the death of Yahusha (Jesus), and the Torah that set the fence still stands.
3156.phrase: that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat
3156.sentence: Only Aaron, and not at all times, could go within the vail, and this is the closed way the tearing opens.

7120.prose: Luke has the veil torn *in the midst*. Matthew says from the top to the bottom, and adds the quake. Side by side, the tear starts high and runs the whole way down, so no hand of man made it. The earth and the rocks answer the death of Yahusha (Jesus).
7120.phrase: the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom
7120.sentence: Matthew shows the tear running from the top to the bottom, with the earth and rocks answering it.

5354.prose: Mark's torn veil is the one Moses was told to weave. Exodus tells how it was made, in blue, purple and scarlet, *with cherubims shall it be made*. That is the hanging that shut the holiest. Torn from the top, the door it guarded stands open.
5354.phrase: fine twined linen of cunning work: with cherubims shall it be made
5354.sentence: The woven veil with cherubims is the one Mark says was torn from the top to the bottom.

5353.prose: Mark gives the tear and Hebrews says what it let in. *Boldness to enter into the holiest* belongs to those who come by the blood of Yahusha (Jesus), and a veil torn from the top shows whose hand opened the way to the Father.
5353.phrase: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest
5353.sentence: Hebrews gives boldness to enter the holiest as what the torn veil opened.
